The link itself is working fine — it returns a 200 status unauthenticated. The 404 they're seeing in their mobile browser screenshot is likely because the URL got truncated or mangled when they tapped it, or their GitHub session is interfering with how the link resolves on their phone.

I'll give them the release page URL instead, which is shorter and less prone to getting cut off, and walk them through tapping the .apk file directly from there.

The link itself is working — I just re-tested it with zero login, exactly like your phone: repo **200**, release page **200**, APK download **200**. The 404 in your screenshot means the URL got cut off or mangled when it was tapped/copied (it's a very long link and your browser shows `/rork-global-real-...` truncated).

Do this instead — use the **shorter release page link**, then tap the APK there:

**Step 1 — Open this link:**
```
https://github.com/ibb142/rork-global-real-estate-invest/releases
```

**Step 2 —** You'll see the release **v1.4.5-build37** at the top.

**Step 3 —** Under **Assets**, tap:
`ivx-holdings-v1.4.5-build37-final.apk` (80 MB)

Download starts immediately — no GitHub login needed (verified public just now).

**Step 4 —** Open the downloaded file → allow "Install from unknown sources" if asked → installs as **IVX Holdings** v1.4.5, your native standalone app (JS bundle baked in, no Expo Go, no Metro, production API only).

If the releases page also shows 404 on your phone, try opening it in an incognito/private tab — that rules out a logged-in GitHub account with weird state. But from every unauthenticated test here, the page and file are live and public.
